what: The Long Division Calculator shows long division worked out step by step, in the same layout you write on paper. Type the dividend and divisor and the quotient appears above the line, with every multiply-and-subtract step below it and each digit that is brought down marked in green.

Choose an answer with a remainder, also shown as a mixed number and a decimal, or with decimals to 2, 3, 4, 6 or 10 places, or until the answer ends or repeats. Repeating digits are marked with a line on top. Decimal divisors are handled by moving the decimal point, with a note explaining it.
Under the working, numbered steps explain each part in plain words, so students can follow how the answer was found, not just what it is.
uses: Check long division answers and see where a mistake happened.
Follow each divide, multiply, subtract and bring-down step.
Show worked examples in class in the layout your school uses.
Turn a fraction into a decimal and see if it repeats.
See the quotient and remainder with a check sum.
tutorial: This is the number being divided, such as 7452 or 18.5.
This is the number you divide by, such as 6 or 0.25.
Pick "With remainder" for whole-number answers or "With decimals" to keep going.
For decimal answers, choose how many places, or "Until it ends or repeats".
Choose Bus stop or European to match the way you learned it.
Follow the numbered explanation and compare it with the written working.
features: Bus stop or European style, with lines and brought-down digits.
Shown as a remainder, a mixed number and a decimal.
Up to 10 places, or until the answer ends or repeats.
Detected and marked with a line.
Converted step by step with an explanation.
Divided without the signs, with the sign rule explained.
Copy the answer and all the steps as text.

example.title: Worked example: 1000 ÷ 7
example.text: Type 1000 and 7 and choose "With remainder". 7 goes into 10 once (7), leaving 3; bring down 0 to make 30. 7 goes into 30 four times (28), leaving 2; bring down 0 to make 20. 7 goes into 20 twice (14), leaving 6. The answer is 142 remainder 6, or 142 6/7. Switch to "With decimals" and "Until it ends or repeats" to see 142.857142 with 857142 repeating.

tips: Remember the order: divide, multiply, subtract, bring down, and repeat.
Check your answer: quotient × divisor + remainder should equal the dividend.
If a subtraction gives a number bigger than the divisor, the quotient digit was too small.
Estimate first: 7452 ÷ 6 is a bit more than 7000 ÷ 6, so around 1200.
problems: Division by 0 has no answer. Check the divisor.
When either number has decimals, a remainder does not make sense, so the answer is given with decimals.
Long numbers make wide layouts. Scroll sideways inside the working area on a phone.
